about: Third refresh of 2026-11-15: the dying-face study, rounds 1 and 2 (NB 'how a face dies (the first look, reviewed)', 'a death is a dip that keeps going'; CLAIMS DY1-DY7), the 4 x 5 empty patch rerun on the CPU (NB addendum; CLAIMS GP10), the second card (NB 'a second card'; CLAIMS GL1, GL2, notes on SH3, SH4). Each item: value (numbers drawn on the page), quote (copied from research/NOTEBOOK.md or research/CLAIMS.md, or from the file named in 'file'; collect.py checks that it occurs there and that each value occurs in it), src. Round 3 of the dying-face study is under review and is not used.

fade.quote: It stays at its stationary density until about 20 generations before death and then fades over the whole face
fade.src: NB 2026-11-15, how a face dies; CLAIMS DY1 (A)

plunge.quote: the final plunge has median 6, 6, 7, 7 generations in the four groups although lifetimes differ by e^6.5

lopsided.quote: at half population 32–39% are more lopsided than 95% of randomly thinned stationary faces (9–11% in a control 64 generations earlier)

rim.quote: stationary rim-row occupancy 0.512 free against 0.349, 0.323, 0.298 tied (csz, c2v, D2h)

nu07.quote: dips to 0.7 of the mean come at ln ν = −4.16, −3.80, −3.77, −3.74 per face per generation in c1, csz, c2v, D2h (review −4.16, −3.80, −3.78, −3.88)

often.quote: Dips to 0.7 P̄ come about once per 60 generations per face and equally often whatever the ties
often.src: NB 2026-11-15, a death is a dip that keeps going

part.quote: the groups part below about 0.6 of the mean

pstar.quote: The point of no return (q = 1/2) is at 0.079, 0.114, 0.152, 0.245 of the mean (about 2.5 live cells of 31 in the untied face)

births.quote: births per empty cell 0.90–0.91 of stationary at lag 16, survival 0.98–0.99; 0.45 and 0.88 at lag 8

forecasts.quote: Before the first look I wrote six forecasts of how a face dies and before the second seven more. One of the thirteen held, the dullest: that shallow dips follow a bell curve.
forecasts.src: the essay, 'How a face dies' and 'Where I was wrong'; NB 2026-11-15 (L2-L7 failed; round 2: one of seven held)

corrections.said: A face's population falls in steps as equal as those of ln τ, one per tied edge
corrections.by: a reviewer, with its own stepper (REVIEW-dying)
corrections.quote: The study wrote that the population falls in steps as equal as those of ln τ; the steps are −2.35, −2.62, −2.77 while ln τ's are −2.18, −2.17, −2.12.

corrections.said: A live cell lost at a tied edge costs 0.86 in ln τ, twice the 0.436 per live cell of the untied face
corrections.now: 0.93, 0.83, 0.77 along the ladder (0.64–1.00 over three vessels); 0.436 was an average, not a marginal
corrections.by: a reviewer, with its own stepper (REVIEW-dying)

corrections.said: Below half its population a face pays a constant price per further cell lost, 5.5 + 3.4 per free edge
corrections.now: The tail is close to straight but not straight; the step per free edge ranges from 3.0 to 4.5 with the fit window
corrections.by: a reviewer, with its own stepper (REVIEW-dying, round 2)
corrections.quote: The review reproduces the slopes (15.55, 12.57, 9.19, 5.51) and does not confirm the reading

audits.label: Adversarial review of the dying-face study (rounds 1 and 2)
audits.line: Own stepper matched to the oracle on twelve systems, fresh seeds; the fade and the point of no return confirmed, four readings withdrawn.

audits.label: Review of the GTX 1080's first report
audits.line: No GPU: the guard exercised on the CPU, a third code for the 4 × 4 torus; the anchor on file was a high draw.

milestones.text: A face watched as it dies: no erosion from an edge
A death is a dip that keeps going
